## claude.ai Honeycomb
Honeycomb MCP Server - Observability Data Query Interface

<role>
You are an observability assistant for Honeycomb users. You investigate production behavior — performance, errors, deployment impact, alert state — by querying real telemetry through these tools. The workspace's actual state is only knowable through tool calls; do not reason from priors about what services, datasets, or alerts exist.

When the user names a dataset, span, or service, treat it as a starting point for discovery, not a license to skip it. The right span name within a dataset is rarely obvious from the dataset name alone, and aggregating the wrong attribute or the wrong span is the most common cause of misleading answers.
</role>

<workflow>
For most observability questions — including "how many", "what's slow", "what's erroring" — start with span discovery (list_spans, get_span_details). These tools return counts and attribute distributions directly; they often answer the question without a follow-up query. Reach for run_query only when you need a calculation, distribution, or comparison those tools can't express. Span tools work across all trace-aware datasets in scope without needing to know which dataset to target.

1. ORIENT
   - Call 'get_workspace_context' to learn the team, environments, and dataset counts. Use the returned environment slug in subsequent calls.

2. DISCOVER (pick the path that matches the question)
   - Span discovery — for "what's happening / what's slow / how many X / what does service X do":
     - 'list_spans' ranks span names by count with root_count to distinguish entry points from internal helpers. Counts here are often the answer to "how many X happened".
     - 'get_span_details' on a chosen span_name returns its populated attributes, value cardinality, and top observed values — including which spans actually populate a count-bearing attribute.
     Answer directly from these when you can — composing an equivalent run_query by hand is slower and more error-prone.

58	// else an explicit-choice error) supplies the subject token — exchanged at
59	// that context's core, never at the active context's. Token calls then only
60	// exchange (through repocreds, the same code path and wire form
61	// git-remote-entire uses), re-minting an expired login JWT from the stored
62	// refresh token as needed — so a poller's re-mints don't depend on
63	// discovery staying reachable.
64	type RepoTokenSource struct {
65		creds *repocreds.Cache
66	}

68	// NewRepoTokenSource resolves clusterHost's trusted core and login context
69	// and returns a source minting tokens for that cluster.
70	func NewRepoTokenSource(ctx context.Context, clusterHost string) (*RepoTokenSource, error) {
71		if clusterHost == "" {
72			return nil, errors.New("repo-scoped token exchange requires a target cluster host")
73		}
74	
75		httpClient := &http.Client{Timeout: repoExchangeTimeout, Transport: repoExchangeTransportForTest}
76		clusterCtx, err := resolveContextForCluster(ctx, userdirs.Config(), userdirs.Cache(), clusterHost, httpClient, nil)
77		if err != nil {
78			return nil, err
79		}
80	
81		allowInsecure := insecureHTTPEnabled() || isLoopbackHTTP(clusterCtx.CoreURL)
82		loginProvider, err := NewRefreshingLoginProvider(clusterCtx, repoExchangeTransportForTest, allowInsecure)

87		return &RepoTokenSource{creds: repocreds.New(clusterCtx.CoreURL, "https://"+clusterHost, loginProvider, httpClient)}, nil

90	// Token returns a repo-scoped token for repoSlug (the surface-prefixed repo
91	// path, e.g. /gh/octocat/hello, joined verbatim to the cluster URL to form
92	// the audience) and action ("pull" or "push"). Tokens are cached per
93	// (repoSlug, action) until near expiry.

103				return "", fmt.Errorf("repo-scoped token exchange: %w: %w", ErrRepoTargetUnknown, err)

105			return "", fmt.Errorf("repo-scoped token exchange: %w", err)
106		}
107		return token, nil
108	}
109	
110	// Invalidate drops the cached (repoSlug, action) token so the next Token
111	// call re-exchanges — for when the data plane rejected it (401) ahead of
112	// its recorded expiry.
113	func (s *RepoTokenSource) Invalidate(repoSlug, action string) {
114		s.creds.Invalidate(repoSlug, action)
115	}
116	
117	// RepoScopedToken is the one-shot form of RepoTokenSource: resolve, mint
118	// once, discard. Callers that re-mint (e.g. a polling wait) should hold a
119	// RepoTokenSource instead, so re-mints skip cluster discovery.
120	func RepoScopedToken(ctx context.Context, clusterHost, repoSlug, action string) (string, error) {
121		src, err := NewRepoTokenSource(ctx, clusterHost)
122		if err != nil {
123			return "", err
124		}
125		return src.Token(ctx, repoSlug, action)
126	}

62	// responds with a non-200 status. Callers can errors.As it to surface
63	// status-specific UX (e.g. a friendly 403 message) or branch on the
64	// RFC 6749 error code.
65	type OAuthError struct {
66		Status int
67		Code   string // RFC 6749 `error` code from the response body; "" when not present
68		Body   string
69	}

71	func (e *OAuthError) Error() string {

75	// PostOAuthToken posts a form-encoded request to coreURL+"/oauth/token"
76	// and parses the standard {access_token, expires_in} response. Callers
77	// build the form (grant_type, subject_token, audience, etc.) so the
78	// helper stays neutral about which OAuth grant is being exercised.
79	//
80	// If the form carries client_id (and optionally client_secret), the
81	// helper lifts both into an HTTP Basic Authorization header and drops
82	// them from the form body. zitadel/oidc's token endpoint reads client
83	// credentials only from Basic auth, so form-only client_id produces
84	// invalid_client even when the form is otherwise well-formed. Both values
85	// are url.QueryEscaped per RFC 6749 §2.3.1 because pkg/op QueryUnescapes
86	// them on the other side — a raw '+'/'%xx' would round-trip to a different
87	// value and fail invalid_client (matches core/api/token_endpoint.go).
88	//
89	// coreURL must already be trimmed of any trailing slash. A non-200
90	// response is surfaced as *OAuthError (RFC 6749 defines token-endpoint
91	// success as 200 only); transport and decode failures
92	// are wrapped plain errors.
93	func PostOAuthToken(ctx context.Context, httpClient *http.Client, coreURL string, form url.Values) (accessToken string, expiresIn int, err error) {
94		clientID := form.Get("client_id")
95		clientSecret := form.Get("client_secret")
96		if clientID != "" {
97			form = cloneValuesWithoutClient(form)
98		}
99	
100		req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodPost,
101			coreURL+"/oauth/token", strings.NewReader(form.Encode()))
102		if err != nil {
103			return "", 0, fmt.Errorf("build token request: %w", err)
104		}
105		req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded")
106		if clientID != "" {
107			// RFC 6749 §2.3.1: percent-encode before Basic so pkg/op's
108			// QueryUnescape recovers the original (matches token_endpoint.go).
109			req.SetBasicAuth(url.QueryEscape(clientID), url.QueryEscape(clientSecret))
110		}
111	
112		resp, err := httpClient.Do(req)
113		if err != nil {
114			return "", 0, fmt.Errorf("token request: %w", err)
115		}
116		defer resp.Body.Close()
117	
118		if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
119			msg, _ := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, 1024)) //nolint:errcheck // best-effort body read for error message
120			var oauthBody struct {
121				Code string `json:"error"`
122			}
123			_ = json.Unmarshal(msg, &oauthBody) //nolint:errcheck // best-effort code extraction; non-JSON bodies leave Code empty
124			return "", 0, &OAuthError{Status: resp.StatusCode, Code: oauthBody.Code, Body: strings.TrimSpace(string(msg))}
125		}

1	// Command git-remote-entire is the git remote helper for entire:// URLs.
2	//
3	// Git resolves `git clone entire://host/project/repo` by exec'ing a binary
4	// named git-remote-entire on PATH, handing it the remote-helper protocol on
5	// stdin and reading responses from stdout. This is a small, dedicated
6	// binary (no cobra command tree) that shares the protocol, transport, and
7	// auth packages with the main entire CLI.
8	//
9	// IMPORTANT: nothing here may write to stdout except the helper protocol
10	// itself — git parses stdout as a strict pkt-line stream, so a stray banner
11	// or log line corrupts the transfer. Diagnostics go to stderr (and the
12	// ENTIRE_DEBUG-gated debuglog).
13	//
14	// Authentication resolves the login context for the target cluster from the
15	// shared contexts.json: the cluster's cores come from the cluster_cores.json
16	// cache (or a live /.well-known fetch on miss), then the account is selected
17	// from local contexts. It then mints repo-scoped tokens by exchanging that
18	// context's login JWT.

22		"context"
23		"fmt"
24		"io"
25		"net/http"

27		"os"

37		"github.com/entireio/cli/internal/entireclient/httpclient"
38		"github.com/entireio/cli/internal/entireclient/repocreds"
39		"github.com/entireio/cli/internal/entireclient/userdirs"
40		"github.com/entireio/cli/internal/remotehelper"
41		"github.com/entireio/cli/internal/remotehelper/debuglog"
42		"github.com/entireio/cli/internal/remotehelper/githelper"

44		"github.com/entireio/cli/internal/remotehelper/transport"

51	func run(args []string) int {

53		// length 2). Git always invokes the helper as

55		// never collide with a real remote-helper invocation.

63		if len(args) < 3 {

65			return 128

163	// loadedVersion populates the build info and returns the resolved version.
164	func loadedVersion() string {
165		versioninfo.Load()
166		return versioninfo.Version
167	}
168	
169	// infoFlagText renders the output for the standalone --version / --help flags,
170	// returning false for anything else. Kept pure (version passed in, no globals)
171	// so it's unit-testable.
172	func infoFlagText(flag, version string) (string, bool) {
173		switch flag {
174		case "--version":
175			return fmt.Sprintf("%s %s\nGo version: %s\nOS/Arch: %s/%s\n",
176				remotehelper.BinaryName, version, runtime.Version(), runtime.GOOS, runtime.GOARCH), true
177		case "--help":
178			return fmt.Sprintf("%s %s\n\n"+
179				"This is a helper which Git calls when encountering entire://... URLs.  "+
180				"For more information see https://github.com/entireio/cli.\n",
181				remotehelper.BinaryName, version), true
182		}
183		return "", false
184	}
185	
186	// resolveProtocolVersion reads the effective protocol.version from
187	// the GIT_PROTOCOL environment variable. The value is a colon-
188	// separated list of key=value pairs (e.g. "version=2"). We accept
189	// 0, 1, or 2; any other value emits a stderr warning and falls
190	// back to 2 — upstream Git's default since 2.26.
191	func resolveProtocolVersion() int {
192		return parseProtocolVersion(os.Getenv("GIT_PROTOCOL"), os.Stderr)
193	}
194	
195	func parseProtocolVersion(raw string, warn io.Writer) int {
196		const defaultVersion = 2
197		for kv := range strings.SplitSeq(raw, ":") {
198			k, v, ok := strings.Cut(kv, "=")
199			if !ok || k != "version" {
200				continue
201			}
202			switch v {
203			case "0":
204				return 0
205			case "1":
206				return 1
207			case "2":
208				return 2
209			}
210			fmt.Fprintf(warn, "git-remote-entire: ignoring unrecognised protocol.version=%q; defaulting to %d\n", v, defaultVersion)
211			return defaultVersion
212		}

216	// resolveCreds builds the repo-scoped token cache, choosing the auth source:
217	//
218	//   - ENTIRE_TOKEN set: use the env JWT verbatim as the login token, deriving
219	//     the login server URL from its aud claim. Skips contexts.json and the keyring
220	//     entirely — the CI / workload-identity path. A non-URL aud is a hard

222	//   - otherwise: resolve the login context for this cluster from contexts.json

228		// fallback to context auth, which would mask a misconfigured CI runner.
229		// Read and trim once here, the only place we touch it, so every downstream
230		// consumer (aud derivation and the exchanged subject_token) sees the
231		// cleaned value; a trailing newline from $(cat token) is common. An empty
232		// or whitespace-only value fails closed.
233		if raw, ok := os.LookupEnv(auth.EnvTokenVar); ok {

242		// login servers are taken from the cluster_cores.json cache (or a live
243		// /.well-known fetch on miss/expiry), then the account is selected from
244		// local contexts — active context if eligible, else the sole eligible
245		// one, else an explicit-choice error.
246		cfgDir := userdirs.Config()
247		clusterCtx, err := clusterdiscovery.ResolveContextForCluster(ctx, cfgDir, userdirs.Cache(), parsedURL.Host, httpClient, debuglog.Printf)
248		if err != nil {
249			return nil, err //nolint:wrapcheck // ResolveContextForCluster already returns a user-facing error; preserved verbatim for the "fatal: <msg>" surface
250		}
251	
252		// The login-JWT provider transparently refreshes an expired login JWT
253		// from the stored refresh token (serialised across processes, rotated
254		// tokens persisted) before repocreds exchanges it for repo-scoped tokens.
255		loginProvider, err := auth.NewRefreshingLoginProvider(clusterCtx, httpClient.Transport, skipTLS)
256		if err != nil {
257			return nil, err //nolint:wrapcheck // NewRefreshingLoginProvider already returns a user-facing error
258		}

260		// Mint repo-scoped tokens by exchanging the context's login JWT at its
261		// login server's /oauth/token, cached per (repo, action) for this invocation.
262		return repocreds.New(clusterCtx.CoreURL, clusterBaseURL, loginProvider, httpClient), nil
263	}
264	
265	// resolveEnvTokenCreds builds the repo-cred cache for the ENTIRE_TOKEN path.
266	// Split out of resolveCreds with explicit clusterHost/cacheDir params (no
267	// os.Getenv / userdirs.Cache globals) so the trust gate below is unit-testable
268	// against a fake well-known server.
269	//
270	// SECURITY: coreURL is derived from the env token's *unverified* aud claim, and
271	// it becomes the host the token is POSTed to as a subject_token during
272	// exchange. Before trusting it, we confirm the core is one the target cluster
273	// actually advertises — anchored to the clone URL's host the user typed (TLS to
274	// its /.well-known/entire-cluster.json), not to the token's own claims. Without
275	// this gate a forged aud could redirect the token to an attacker-chosen host.
276	//
277	// The gate is only as strong as that TLS verification: with
278	// ENTIRE_TLS_SKIP_VERIFY=true (a local-dev escape hatch) the well-known fetch
279	// is no longer authenticated, so a MITM could advertise an attacker host as a
280	// trusted core. Do not combine ENTIRE_TOKEN with ENTIRE_TLS_SKIP_VERIFY in
281	// CI / workload-identity environments.
282	func resolveEnvTokenCreds(ctx context.Context, envToken, clusterHost, clusterBaseURL, cacheDir string, httpClient *http.Client) (*repocreds.Cache, error) {
283		coreURL, err := auth.CoreURLFromEnvToken(envToken)
284		if err != nil {
285			return nil, err //nolint:wrapcheck // CoreURLFromEnvToken already returns a user-facing, ENTIRE_TOKEN-prefixed error
286		}
287		cores, err := clusterdiscovery.ResolveClusterCores(ctx, cacheDir, clusterHost, httpClient, debuglog.Printf)
288		if err != nil {
289			return nil, err //nolint:wrapcheck // ResolveClusterCores returns a user-facing discovery error
290		}
291		if !coreTrusted(coreURL, cores) {
292			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s aud %q is not a trusted login server for cluster %s (advertised: %s); the token belongs to a different cluster",
293				auth.EnvTokenVar, coreURL, clusterHost, strings.Join(cores, ", "))
294		}
295		debuglog.Printf("authenticating via %s; core=%s", auth.EnvTokenVar, coreURL)
296		return repocreds.New(coreURL, clusterBaseURL, func(context.Context) (string, error) {
297			return envToken, nil
298		}, httpClient), nil
299	}
300	
301	// coreTrusted reports whether coreURL is in the cluster's advertised core
302	// set, comparing on trailing-slash-insensitive equality to match how core
303	// URLs are compared elsewhere (contexts.ContextsForIssuer, auth.sameIssuer).
304	func coreTrusted(coreURL string, trusted []string) bool {
305		want := strings.TrimRight(coreURL, "/")
306		for _, t := range trusted {
307			if strings.TrimRight(t, "/") == want {
308				return true
309			}
310		}
311		return false
312	}
313	
314	// gitActionFromRequest classifies a smart-HTTP request as "pull" or "push"
315	// so the right repo-scoped token can be minted. Returns "" when the
316	// endpoint isn't a recognised git smart-HTTP route.
317	func gitActionFromRequest(req *http.Request) string {
318		path := req.URL.Path
319		switch req.Method {
320		case http.MethodPost:
321			switch {
322			case strings.HasSuffix(path, "/git-receive-pack"):
323				return "push"
324			case strings.HasSuffix(path, "/git-upload-pack"):
325				return "pull"
326			}
327		case http.MethodGet:
328			if strings.HasSuffix(path, "/info/refs") {
329				switch req.URL.Query().Get("service") {
330				case "git-receive-pack":
331					return "push"
332				case "git-upload-pack":
333					return "pull"
334				}
335			}
336		}
337		return ""
338	}
339	
340	// installSignals ties HTTP request lifetimes to the parent git process.
341	// Ctrl-C delivers SIGINT to the whole foreground process group (us
342	// included); cancelling ctx aborts in-flight transfers instead of waiting
343	// out the read timeout. After the first signal we unhook so a second
344	// Ctrl-C hits the runtime default and hard-exits.
345	func installSignals() (context.Context, context.CancelFunc) {
346		ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
347		go func() {
348			<-ctx.Done()
349			stop()
350			time.Sleep(2 * time.Second)
351			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "git-remote-entire: shutdown taking longer than expected; press Ctrl-C again to force-quit")
352		}()
353		return ctx, stop
354	}

naming the correct host and the corrected `git clone entire://...` URL.
